newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--Some 6,500 state-held properties are to go under the hammer to cover the gap noted in revenues and targets in state revenues. Deputy Finance Minister George Drys said yesterday.

--An expert committee inquiring into pensions in the farmers' pension fund OGA has found that one in five pensions are given on the basis of disability. The high figure is attributed to abuse of the law on approving disability pensions, and doctors have been blamed.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis's recently-announced changes to the pension and labour sectors will be the focus of talks between ministries and unions and employers, the government said yesterday. Source say the plans announced by Simitis in effect threw down the gauntlet to unions to come to terms with new realities.

--Greek investors in Bulgaria said yesterday that they would not abandon the country, despite the current economic crisis. The 350 Greek firms active in Bulgaria constitute 13 percent of total investment and employ 25,000 people.
--Simitis's new model of labour relations and goal of "a worker willing to compromise" has drawn opposition from the left.
--Greece will be participating in the OSCE's protection force to Albania. The OSCE decision must be cleared by the United Nations.

--Albanian President Sali Berisha is reportedly arming ethnic Albanians in Kosovo and the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia while other reports mention the distribution of circulars calling for a 'Greater Albania'.

--Armed Albanians wanting visas attacked the Greek consulate at Gjirokaster with automatic weapons and tear gas yesterday. The crowd broke down the gate and threatened consular staff although there were no injuries.
--Concern on the island of Crete after reported instances of mad cow disease affecting two middle-aged men.

--New conservation opposition New Democracy party leader Costas Karamanlis is busy mending fences after his election on Friday: yesterday he had a warm meeting with former premier and ND heavyweight Constantine Mitsotakis, while there are reports of talks under way to bring Antonis Samaras, leader of the breakaway Political Spring party, back into the ND fold.

--Veteran Communist Harilaos Florakis is in excellent condition following surgery to remove an aneurism; ironically, he is recuperating a few beds away from ailing former dictator George Papadopoulos.
--The development ministry is determined to put an end to credit card scams which have recently come to light. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
